links.comparator_used: Physician profiles with explicit non-AI disclosure (and across AI use types: administrative, diagnostic, therapeutic) rather than AI use being undisclosed
links.outcome: Physician perception (competence, trust, empathy) and care-seeking/appointment willingness
links.effect: Administrative AI disclosure rated more favorably than diagnostic and therapeutic AI disclosure; under high severity, therapeutic AI disclosure amplified negative responses and explicit non-AI disclosure was associated with greater appointment willingness (1574 adults, 5 × 2 factorial; no effect sizes in abstract).
links.tradeoff: Disclosing clinical (diagnostic/therapeutic) AI use lowered perceived physician quality and care-seeking intention, especially for high-severity conditions; effects were mediated by competence, trust and empathy (exploratory).
links.quote: High-severity conditions amplified negative responses to therapeutic AI, whereas explicit non-AI disclosure was associated with greater appointment willingness under high severity.
